saints.name: Tarasius
saints.legacy: Defender of icons and Church integrity
saints.summary: Tarasius was the Patriarch of Constantinople from 784 to 806, known for his strong defense of the veneration of icons during the Iconoclast controversy. He was a man of great virtue and simplicity, leading a life of prayer and service while refusing to compromise his principles, even in the face of imperial pressure. His legacy includes a commitment to the integrity of the Church and the promotion of holy images, which was affirmed by the Second Council of Nicaea.
